title: Impact of 2003 Dividend Tax Cut on Corporate Dividend Payouts

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with firm and year fixed effects.
- Why: The 2003 dividend tax cut is a common time shock. Firms with higher exposure to the tax cut (treated) should differentially change dividend payouts after 2003 relative to less-exposed firms (controls). DID captures this differential change controlling for time-invariant firm heterogeneity (firm FE) and aggregate shocks (year FE).
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the tax cut, dividend payout trends for high- and low-exposure firms would have evolved similarly.
  - No anticipation: Firms did not adjust dividends in anticipation before the policy’s effective date.
  - Stable composition/SUTVA: No spillovers across firms; treatment status is stable over time.
- Interpretation: With log dividends as the outcome, the DID coefficient on treated × post is the log-point change; exp(beta) − 1 gives the percent change in payouts for treated vs control post-2003.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Ensure required package is available
req_pkgs <- c("fixest")
to_install <- req_pkgs[!sapply(req_pkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if(length(to_install) > 0) install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")

library(fixest)

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s33_data.csv")

# Basic cleaning/types
df$unit_id <- as.integer(df$unit_id)
df$period  <- as.integer(df$period)
df$treated <- as.integer(df$treated)
df$post    <- as.integer(df$post)
df$y       <- as.numeric(df$y)

# Sanity checks
if(!all(df$treated %in% c(0,1))) stop("treated must be 0/1.")
if(!all(df$post %in% c(0,1))) stop("post must be 0/1.")
if(length(unique(df$period)) < 2) stop("Need at least two periods for DID.")
if(length(unique(df$unit_id)) < 2) stop("Need multiple firms for DID.")

# Create interaction (not relying on provided treat_x_post)
df$treat_x_post <- df$treated * df$post

# 2) Main DID: firm FE + year FE, cluster by firm
m_did <- feols(y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)

# Extract main effect
beta  <- coef(m_did)[["treated:post"]]
se_b  <- se(m_did)[["treated:post"]]
p_b   <- pvalue(m_did)[["treated:post"]]
ci_b  <- confint(m_did, "treated:post", level = 0.95)
pct_b <- (exp(beta) - 1) * 100

# 3) Robustness A: Two-way clustered SE (firm and year)
m_did_2c <- feols(y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id + period)
beta_2c  <- coef(m_did_2c)[["treated:post"]]
se_2c    <- se(m_did_2c)[["treated:post"]]
p_2c     <- pvalue(m_did_2c)[["treated:post"]]
ci_2c    <- confint(m_did_2c, "treated:post", level = 0.95)
pct_2c   <- (exp(beta_2c) - 1) * 100

# 4) Robustness B: Allow treated-specific linear trend
df$period_c <- as.numeric(scale(df$period, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE))
m_trend <- feols(y ~ treated:post + treated:period_c | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)
beta_trend <- coef(m_trend)[["treated:post"]]
se_trend   <- se(m_trend)[["treated:post"]]
p_trend    <- pvalue(m_trend)[["treated:post"]]
ci_trend   <- confint(m_trend, "treated:post", level = 0.95)
pct_trend  <- (exp(beta_trend) - 1) * 100

# 5) Robustness C: Event-study pre-trend test
# Use the last pre period as reference
if(any(df$post == 0)) {
  ref_pre <- max(df$period[df$post == 0], na.rm = TRUE)
  # Dynamic interactions of calendar year dummies with treated; FE absorb main period and firm effects
  m_es <- feols(y ~ i(period, treated, ref = ref_pre) | unit_id + period, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)

  # Identify pre-period coefficients (periods < ref_pre)
  coefs_es <- coef(m_es)
  nm_es <- names(coefs_es)
  # Extract period numbers from names like "period::2002#treated"
  extract_period <- function(x) {
    as.numeric(sub(".*::(-?[0-9]+)#.*", "\\1", x))
  }
  is_treated_term <- grepl("#treated", nm_es)
  peri_vals <- suppressWarnings(sapply(nm_es, extract_period))
  pre_idx <- which(is_treated_term & !is.na(peri_vals) & peri_vals < ref_pre)

  pretrend_p <- NA
  if(length(pre_idx) > 0) {
    wt <- wald(m_es, keep = nm_es[pre_idx])
    pretrend_p <- wt$p.value
  }
} else {
  pretrend_p <- NA
}

# 6) Robustness D: Placebo DID within pre-periods only
placebo_beta <- placebo_se <- placebo_p <- placebo_pct <- NA
if(any(df$post == 0)) {
  df_pre <- df[df$post == 0, ]
  pre_years <- sort(unique(df_pre$period))
  if(length(pre_years) >= 2) {
    # Define a placebo cutoff at the median pre-year
    placebo_cut <- pre_years[ceiling(length(pre_years)/2)]
    df_pre$placebo_post <- as.integer(df_pre$period >= placebo_cut)
    m_placebo <- feols(y ~ treated:placebo_post | unit_id + period, data = df_pre, cluster = ~ unit_id)
    if("treated:placebo_post" %in% names(coef(m_placebo))) {
      placebo_beta <- coef(m_placebo)[["treated:placebo_post"]]
      placebo_se   <- se(m_placebo)[["treated:placebo_post"]]
      placebo_p    <- pvalue(m_placebo)[["treated:placebo_post"]]
      placebo_pct  <- (exp(placebo_beta) - 1) * 100
    }
  }
}

# 7) Print results
cat("Main DID (FE: firm + year; cluster by firm)\n")
cat(sprintf("  DID log-coefficient (treated x post): %.4f\n", beta))
cat(sprintf("  SE: %.4f, p-value: %.4f, 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", se_b, p_b, ci_b[1], ci_b[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Implied percent change: %.2f%%\n\n", pct_b))

cat("Robustness A: Two-way clustered SE (firm, year)\n")
cat(sprintf("  DID log-coefficient: %.4f\n", beta_2c))
cat(sprintf("  SE: %.4f, p-value: %.4f, 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", se_2c, p_2c, ci_2c[1], ci_2c[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Implied percent change: %.2f%%\n\n", pct_2c))

cat("Robustness B: Add treated-specific linear trend\n")
cat(sprintf("  DID log-coefficient: %.4f\n", beta_trend))
cat(sprintf("  SE: %.4f, p-value: %.4f, 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", se_trend, p_trend, ci_trend[1], ci_trend[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Implied percent change: %.2f%%\n\n", pct_trend))

cat("Robustness C: Event-study pre-trend joint test\n")
if(is.na(pretrend_p)) {
  cat("  Not available (insufficient pre-period variation).\n\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf("  Joint test that all pre-treatment dynamic effects = 0: p-value = %.4f\n\n", pretrend_p))
}

cat("Robustness D: Placebo DID within pre-periods\n")
if(is.na(placebo_beta)) {
  cat("  Not available (insufficient pre-periods).\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf("  Placebo log-coefficient: %.4f, SE: %.4f, p-value: %.4f\n", placebo_beta, placebo_se, placebo_p))
  cat(sprintf("  Implied percent change: %.2f%%\n", placebo_pct))
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Firms more exposed to the 2003 dividend tax cut should raise dividend payouts more than less-exposed firms after 2003.
- Magnitude: For log dividends, an effect around 0.15–0.25 log points (roughly 16–28%) for high-exposure firms relative to low-exposure firms is plausible, consistent with the historically documented post-2003 rise in dividend payouts and initiations among firms with greater tax-sensitive ownership. Robustness checks should yield similar positive effects, with no significant pre-trends or placebo effects.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log dividend payouts before and after 2003 between treated and untreated firms.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Firms with higher exposure to the dividend tax cut reduced their dividend payouts.
